candidates.lead: A tribunal found Rachel Claire Lemonofides racially discriminated against the patient
candidates.evidence_text: A paramedic has been struck off for telling a woman suffering a stroke to stop acting "like a baby" and accused of them of lying about their pain The Healthcare Professionals Tribunal Service heard Rachel Claire Lemonofides made "inappropriate and degrading" comments heard on a 999 call at the woman's home in 2024 It found Lemonofides was guilty of racially motivated discrimination on the grounds of ethnicity and breached professional boundaries The patient underwent emergency surgery at Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester, and was diagnosed with a brain bleed and abdominal aortic aneurysm. North West Ambulance Service said all patients were "entitled to be treated with dignity and respect" The service added: "There is no place within our organisation for colleagues who do not uphold those values." The tribunal was told the paramedic was one of a team of two who responded in January 2024 to a 999 call from the patient, who felt a sharp pain in her chest, "which became unbearable"

candidates.lead: Police investigate after the Believe Achieve CIC project was targeted on Monday night
candidates.evidence_text: Site for new Bolton community bike hub 'stormed' by vandals - BBC News Image source, Believe Achieve CIC Image caption, The project was given planning permission in July By Jade Taylorson North West Published 1 hour ago A site where a new community bike hub is being built to help reduce antisocial behaviour has been vandalised. Police are investigating after the Believe Achieve CIC project in Stoneclough, Bolton, was targeted on Monday night. The bike hub was being built after reports of young people in the area using illegal motorised bikes - and the group aims to give youngsters access to bicycles while teaching road safety and maintenance skills. Tunde Olasupo, project founder, says the site was "stormed" by people who vandalised a surrounding fence and forcibly opened a container that will house the hub. They added there had been opposition to the project, with concerns about further antisocial behaviour. There were also concerns about its location and environmental impact, Olasupo said. 'Upset' "Of course, I'm upset, and when you see something that you've worked hard for deliberately damaged, you're human, it hurts," he told BBC Radio Manchester. He said the site had been targeted before. "The objective is to balance access and community benefit with protecting and enhancing the natural environment, and that's one of the things that we're trying to make very clear to people." Image source, Believe Achieve CIC Image caption, Tunde Olasupo thanked residents who had shown the project support Believe Achieve CIC was set up in memory of Olasupo's son, Kingsley, who died in 2019, with the aim of giving young people opportunities he never got to experience. Despite the damage, Olasupo said he would not give up on the project. "I've learnt something from Kingsley, that everything that happens… there is always a good thing at the end of the road." candidates.lead: Police say the man is accused of failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity
candidates.evidence_text: Man charged over Manchester synagogue attack - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, The charges are linked to the 2 October 2025 attack By Paul Burnell North West Published 20 August 2026 A man has been charged in connection with the Manchester synagogue attack in which two men were killed. Counter terrorism police said Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim, 49, of St James Road, Higher Broughton, Salford, had been charged with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity. Hakim has been remanded into custody to appear before Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday. There have so far been eight arrests in connection with the attack, however this is the first charge that "relates directly" to the morning of 2 October, when two men died as the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation synagogue was attacked by Jihad Al-Shamie. He was shot by police and died at the scene. Worshippers Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed. Assistant Chief Constable Rob Potts, from Counter Terrorism Policing North West (CTPNW) , said: "This is a significant development in our investigation, and my thoughts are with all those affected by the attack, particularly the bereaved loved ones and survivors. "We have updated them and continue to offer them as much support as possible. "Since the attack took place, we have been unwavering in our commitment to establishing the full picture behind the incident and identifying anybody who may have been involved in any way." In July, Mohammad Bashir, 31, who planned an attack on a military base with the Manchester synagogue attacker was jailed for life with a minimum term of 17 years. He drove his friend Jihad Al-Shamie on a 10-hour round trip to conduct hostile reconnaissance at the UK's Defence Academy in Shrivenham, Oxfordshire, on 14 August 2025. Weeks after that journey, Al-Shamie, 35, was shot dead by police after carrying out the Heaton Park Synagogue attack. candidates.lead: Northern Care Alliance has responded to claims raised by an investigation
candidates.evidence_text: One of the north-west of England's biggest healthcare trusts has responded to allegations it failed to properly investigate claims patients died or were harmed during surgery Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Hospital, was put under an NHS enforcement notice to improve patient safety, in June But whistle blowers have now told an investigation by the Independent and Channel 4 , external that they were discouraged from reporting concerns The trust has told the BBC it is working to address staff concerns and has "clear processes to investigate incidents" A spokesperson for NCA said the trust changed the way it was organised in response to demands by NHS England to improve standards in surgical wards, tackling backlogs in spinal and gynaecology services But the investigation found patients are alleged to have been "left dying or in pain" in overcrowded A&E corridors, before then receiving invasive treatments which might have been avoided if there was no delay, the investigation claims

candidates.lead: Six men are arrested after early morning raids on homes in Salford
candidates.evidence_text: Six men held after Salford raids target heroin and cocaine supply - BBC News Image caption, Six men were arrested in early morning raids By Richard Stead Reporting from in Salford Published 20 August 2026 Six men have been arrested in drugs raids which aimed to target the supply of heroin and crack cocaine in Salford. About 50 police officers were involved in the operation, which took place at five addresses in the Pendlebury and Clifton areas of the city at 0530 BST. Officers seized drugs which are believed to be cocaine and heroin, cash and two high-value mountain bikes, which are suspected to have been stolen. Ch Insp Lee Gridley said the raids were the "result of months of evidence gathering" by Swinton's neighbourhood teams to "take action against people who prey on the vulnerable". He added: "Hopefully this operation will disrupt the supply of Class A drugs across Salford and all we can do is ask communities to give us the information we need and we will act robustly." Image caption, Chief Inspector Lee Gridley urges people to give information to police Police rammed the front doors off their hinges before entering the houses and flats to search the properties and make arrests. Four of the addresses were on Hopwood Street, Pendlebury and the fifth was a flat on Castleway in the Clifton area. Image caption, Part of the operation was on Hopwood Street in Pendlebury Those arrested in the raids are being questioned over a range of suspected offences. They include possession of Class A drugs, possession with intent to supply, possession of an offensive weapon, burglary and failure to appear at court. candidates.lead: A blue plaque has been unveiled in Bowdon to commemorate the life and legacy of William Wood
candidates.evidence_text: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determined social reformers His campaigning laid the groundwork for the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875, which finally banned the practice, but Wood did not live to see the law enacted as he died in 1868 at the age of 85 At the plaque unveiling at his former home in Bowdon, councillor Eve Parker, from Trafford Council, said Wood's "compassion, courage and lasting impact on British history will be remembered for generations to come" "William Wood's story is a remarkable piece of local history, and it's a privilege to honour his life's work," the executive member for leisure, arts, culture and heritage said "From his home in Bowdon, he fought tirelessly against unimaginable cruelty, using his own time and resources to protect vulnerable children across the country."

evidence_packet.lead: A blue plaque has been unveiled in Bowdon to commemorate the life and legacy of William Wood
evidence_packet.summary: A blue plaque has been unveiled in Bowdon to commemorate the life and legacy of William Wood
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determined social reformers His campaigning laid the groundwork for the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875, which finally banned the practice, but Wood did not live to see the law enacted as he died in 1868 at the age of 85 At the plaque unveiling at his former home in Bowdon, councillor Eve Parker, from Trafford Council, said Wood's "compassion, courage and lasting impact on British history will be remembered for generations to come" "William Wood's story is a remarkable piece of local history, and it's a privilege to honour his life's work," the executive member for leisure, arts, culture and heritage said "From his home in Bowdon, he fought tirelessly against unimaginable cruelty, using his own time and resources to protect vulnerable children across the country."

candidates.evidence_text: One of the north-west of England's biggest healthcare trusts has responded to allegations it failed to properly investigate claims patients died or were harmed during surgery Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Hospital, was put under an NHS enforcement notice to improve patient safety, in June But whistle blowers have now told an investigation by the Independent and Channel 4 , external that they were discouraged from reporting concerns The trust has told the BBC it is working to address staff concerns and has "clear processes to investigate incidents" A spokesperson for NCA said the trust changed the way it was organised in response to demands by NHS England to improve standards in surgical wards, tackling backlogs in spinal and gynaecology services But the investigation found patients are alleged to have been "left dying or in pain" in overcrowded A&E corridors, before then receiving invasive treatments which might have been avoided if there was no delay, the investigation claims

candidates.evidence_text: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determined social reformers His campaigning laid the groundwork for the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875, which finally banned the practice, but Wood did not live to see the law enacted as he died in 1868 at the age of 85 At the plaque unveiling at his former home in Bowdon, councillor Eve Parker, from Trafford Council, said Wood's "compassion, courage and lasting impact on British history will be remembered for generations to come" "William Wood's story is a remarkable piece of local history, and it's a privilege to honour his life's work," the executive member for leisure, arts, culture and heritage said "From his home in Bowdon, he fought tirelessly against unimaginable cruelty, using his own time and resources to protect vulnerable children across the country."

candidates.evidence_text: A unique slice of Manchester's musical history - when the "Godmother of rock and roll" performed live at a city railway station - has been commemorated The day Sister Rosetta Tharpe played at the disused station at Whalley Range's Wilbraham Road in May 1964 has been marked with the unveiling of a blue plaque Tharpe, who influenced music legends Chuck Berry, Elvis Presley and Little Richard among others, was recording a show for Granada TV's Blues and Gospel Train, along with greats such as blues giant Muddy Waters The plaque is part of an initiative by social historian and broadcaster Karen Gabay, to place plaques across Manchester, honouring Black musicians who left a mark on the city It was unveiled by Gabay at Manchester Central Convention Complex - the former Manchester Central Railway Station - where Tharpe and fellow musicians boarded the train to take them to Whalley Range The historian explained: "She was one cool sister; that swagger, that strut, the way she played the guitar - so many people who see it for the first time are instantly taken aback."

candidates.evidence_text: Plans to bring an historic theatre back into use have taken a major step forward after new investment was approved Wigan's Royal Court Theatre on King Street will receive part of the £3.7m funding Wigan Council is set to receive from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, to support the borough's economy and community developments The Grade II listed theatre, which closed in 1974 and was used as a bingo hall, nightclub and bar, has already received £1.1m in funding for building works Cllr Dane Anderton said the latest funding will help bring the theatre a step closer to becoming "a vibrant destination for residents and visitors" "The Royal Court Theatre is one of Wigan's most recognisable heritage assets and we're delighted to have secured further funding to continue its revival," cabinet portfolio holder for economic development and regeneration at Wigan Council, said "The £1.1 million already invested has helped secure the building's future by carrying out vital protection and restoration works

The funeral service is set to be held at Salford Cathedral on Friday afternoon Cricket, who was known for his signature bowler hat, wellington boots and the catchphrase 'and there's more', became a TV staple in the 80s, appearing in programmes such as The Good Old Days as well as the Royal Variety Performance. His family have invited fans to celebrate his l Cricket’s youngest son, a former comedian who became a priest, Father Frankie Mulgrew said the Cookstown-born comic asked for the last rites twice, “almost like he asked for an encore”, before he died. He described his father as being “like a light” and said he loved making peopl

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Wigan residents hail extraordinary victory after council U-turns on masterplan - but this was 'just one battle' Bridgewater West has been removed from a local plan - meaning a scheme to turn it into a giant Wigan business park could be scrapped Campaigners say ‘the fight isn’t over’ after Wigan Council U-turned on plans to free up former greenbelt land in Astley for a huge business park Bridgewater West was tipped to become the home of around 540,000 sq ft of ‘employment space’ under the council’s Local Plan. Peel Group, which owns the land, planned to turn the area into a ‘ campus style’ business park, alongside new homes and a Park and Ride Campaigners have opposed the scheme from the start , arguing the open fields separating Astley and Boothstown are ‘vital’ to the local community and wildlife as well as protection from flooding. After a year of disputes, Wigan bosses have now rowed back on the scheme Four ‘controversial’ sites will be removed from the local plan. The document was due to be greenlit for public consultation at a cabinet meeting on Thursday, August 27. However now, The Bell, north of Junction 26, the Moss Industrial Estate extension, a pocket of land West of Win Joanna Allsopp, a high school teacher campaigning for the protection of the land , said the shift was a ‘positive step’

Peel Group, which owns the land, planned to turn the area into a ‘ campus style’ business park, alongside new homes and a Park and Ride Campaigners have opposed the scheme from the start , arguing the open fields separating Astley and Boothstown are ‘vital’ to the local community and wildlife as well as protection from flooding. After a year of disputes, Wigan bosses have now rowed back on the scheme Four ‘controversial’ sites will be removed from the local plan. The document was due to be greenlit for public consultation at a cabinet meeting on Thursday, August 27. Hundreds of bins went uncollected due to their lids being 'open' by millimetres in July, while a row ensued over the council's apparent crackdown on its Now in the latest strange happenings, resident Dave Bresnahan was left baffled by what was caught on his doorbell camera. It’s been going on and on and on and everyone has got absolutely fed up “What happened was I put the bin out and I had been away for a few days. I came back that morning and I thought I would only put the black bin out because the rest weren’t full.” He added: “I went to the shop to get some milk and the blue bin was out. I thought that was a bit strange. I thought maybe the neighbour had put it out.”

The local plan sets out Wigan council's vision for future development in the borough, including, crucially, where building projects are all Town hall bosses have now said they believe they can still meet the borough’s employment needs without building on the land at Bridgewater West, in Astley; west of Winwick Lane, in Lowton; at Aspull Common, in Leigh; and to the north Junction 26 of the M6, near Wigan. News D A Greater Manchester school played host to a special celebration for a charity that has been helping families who have a child with life-threatening or terminal illnesses for the past 40 years. The Rainbow Trust, a children's care charity, hosted a special family fun day at Brads The charity has been established nationally for 40 years, and for 22 years has had its own Manchester Care team supporting local families. Joining the celebration was inspirational fundraiser Dr Michael Josephson MBE , who has raised £500,000 for the Rainbow Trust at his charity The event was an opportunity for those families supported by Rainbow Trust to come together and enjoy some much needed family fun during the school holidays. Children played alongside their siblings and families, and got to enjoy face painting, a treasure hunt, games, arts and cr Among those at the event were Evie and her family, who have been helped by the Rainbow Trust. Evie’s mum Vicky said: "As parents we are caring for Evie 24/7 and having support from Rainbow Trust brings Evie so much joy. Evie was born at 29 weeks and has been very poorly having ha "Without Rainbow Trust and Family Support Worker Emma’s support, life would be a lot more difficult."

Peel Group, which owns the land, planned to turn the area into a ‘ campus style’ business park, alongside new homes and a Park and Ride Campaigners have opposed the scheme from the start , arguing the open fields separating Astley and Boothstown are ‘vital’ to the local community and wildlife as well as protection from flooding. After a year of disputes, Wigan bosses have now rowed back on the scheme Four ‘controversial’ sites will be removed from the local plan. The document was due to be greenlit for public consultation at a cabinet meeting on Thursday, August 27. candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport man puzzled as latest bizarre bin incident caught on doorbell camera What Dave Bresnahan later found out, he said, had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporte In recent weeks, a furore of bin collections across the town and its suburbs has sent residents and councillors into a frenzy. Hundreds of bins went uncollected due to their lids being 'open' by millimetres in July, while a row ensued over the council's apparent crackdown on its Now in the latest strange happenings, resident Dave Bresnahan was left baffled by what was caught on his doorbell camera. Mr Bresnahan said it had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough The resident of Bosden Farm near Hazel Grove told the Manchester Evening News : “I had just gone down to the shops. We have had all this chaos about the bins all over Stockport . It’s been going on and on and on and everyone has got absolutely fed up “What happened was I put the bin out and I had been away for a few days. I came back that morning and I thought I would only put the black bin out because the rest weren’t full.” He added: “I went to the shop to get some milk and the blue bin was out. I thought that was a bit strange. I thought maybe the neighbour had put it out.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan The fight to save Wigan’s greenbelt from concrete jungles may have just been won The removal of the land is a ‘huge and incredibly emotional moment’, campaigners say Comments News Hannah Richardson 18:21, 20 Aug 2026 View 3 Images Bridgewater We Wigan campaigners have achieved a resounding victory after four controversial greenbelt sites were removed from the area's local plan Around five million square metres of employment space across the sites was to be allocated in the document under earlier town hall thinking. The local plan sets out Wigan council's vision for future development in the borough, including, crucially, where building projects are all Town hall bosses have now said they believe they can still meet the borough’s employment needs without building on the land at Bridgewater West, in Astley; west of Winwick Lane, in Lowton; at Aspull Common, in Leigh; and to the north Junction 26 of the M6, near Wigan. While plann Wigan council has also set out its intention to object to a fifth area of development, the Gibfield Park masterplan. The latter scheme has been allocated in the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone policy and has the potential to deliver 500 homes and 375,000sqm of sheds The various schemes have been branded an ‘abomination’, a ‘concrete jungle’ and an ‘obliteration of nature’ by residents demanding developers leave their greenspaces alone

candidates.evidence_text: Crime I stood and watched as GMP raided four new homes at 5am - four things stayed with me "It’s easy to forget the destructive criminality that is the reason for these raids - and the people whose lives it is blighting" Comments News opinion Greta Si I always say to anyone asking about my job that there are highs, and there are lows Highs might be the satisfaction of getting a really complex story over the line; reading positive feedback; a ticket to a show or artist you’ve been dying to see (contingent on a review, of course) All those things felt very far away, standing in the driving rain at 5.30am on August 20, watching a tactical aid officer saw through someone’s front door like a hot knife through butter We were on Hopwood Street in Pendlebury with officers from GMP’s Tactical Aid Unit and the Salford Neighbourhood team, watching them execute four dawn raids on properties suspected to be linked to drug dealing and burglaries in the area, with a fifth taking place in Clifton nearb It meant setting my alarm for 4am, hastily downing a coffee and a muffin on the rain-lashed M60 and rolling into a Salford police station just before 5am

candidates.evidence_text: Cheadle and Cheadle Hulme School opens doors for milestone event for children's charity Rainbow Trust The charity supports the families of children with life-threatenng and terminal illnesses, but doesn't receive any central government funding. News D A Greater Manchester school played host to a special celebration for a charity that has been helping families who have a child with life-threatening or terminal illnesses for the past 40 years. The Rainbow Trust, a children's care charity, hosted a special family fun day at Brads The charity has been established nationally for 40 years, and for 22 years has had its own Manchester Care team supporting local families. Joining the celebration was inspirational fundraiser Dr Michael Josephson MBE , who has raised £500,000 for the Rainbow Trust at his charity The event was an opportunity for those families supported by Rainbow Trust to come together and enjoy some much needed family fun during the school holidays. Children played alongside their siblings and families, and got to enjoy face painting, a treasure hunt, games, arts and cr Among those at the event were Evie and her family, who have been helped by the Rainbow Trust. Evie’s mum Vicky said: "As parents we are caring for Evie 24/7 and having support from Rainbow Trust brings Evie so much joy. Evie was born at 29 weeks and has been very poorly having ha "Without Rainbow Trust and Family Support Worker Emma’s support, life would be a lot more difficult."

News D A Greater Manchester school played host to a special celebration for a charity that has been helping families who have a child with life-threatening or terminal illnesses for the past 40 years. The Rainbow Trust, a children's care charity, hosted a special family fun day at Brads The charity has been established nationally for 40 years, and for 22 years has had its own Manchester Care team supporting local families. Joining the celebration was inspirational fundraiser Dr Michael Josephson MBE , who has raised £500,000 for the Rainbow Trust at his charity The event was an opportunity for those families supported by Rainbow Trust to come toge

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale Partner of man, 31, found dead in Rochdale says 'I want him to be remembered as he was' as murder probe dropped Nathan Haigh died at a flat on Great Howarth on August 11 News Paul Britton Reporter and Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news repo The partner of a man who was found dead at a flat in Rochdale has described him as being 'like the sunshine' in a tribute for him Nathan Haigh, 31, was found unresponsive by emergency services at a flat on Great Howarth, near Wardle, just before 7.40pm last Tuesday (August 11). Police were initially called to the scene over reports of an 'unexpected death' Following Mr Haigh's death, a 37-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder . Detectives said they were exploring 'several lines of enquiries in what initially appeared to be suspicious circumstances' In an update issued on August 19, a Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said that 'following extensive enquiries, detectives have ruled out murder as a line of enquiry.' The woman arrested for murder was released and remains on bail for assault Rebecca Hamer, 36, has now shared a tribute for Mr Haigh. She said she was living with him at the time of his death after they struck up a recent relationship

candidates.evidence_text: Cheshire International DJ turned EncroChat drug trafficker absconds from prison Officers are trying to trace Kyle Chase News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 15:53, 20 Aug 2026 Updated 15:54, 20 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Kyle Chase (Image: Merseyside Police) An international DJ who was unmasked as an EncroChat drug trafficker has absconded from prison, police have said Police in Cheshire have issued an appeal for information over the whereabouts of Kyle Chase, who they said was last seen leaving HMP Thorn Cross in Warrington last Friday (August 14) The now 41-year-old was jailed for 12 years in 2024, at Liverpool Crown Court, which heard he was a 'highly trusted conspirator with extensive involvement in the drug world.' Also known as Kyle Muldoon, he had previously carved out a reputation in the international dance music scene under his DJ name Eldon - a reference to the Eldonian Village where he lived He played shows at festivals and events in the likes of Croatia and Ecuador and opened Spray Shop - a former garage transformed into a dance music nightclub close to Bramley Moore docks in Liverpool - in February 2023

candidates.evidence_text: GCSE results Greater Manchester pupils celebrate GCSE results as one borough shines brightest and schools secure record-breaking year GCSE pupils received their grades this morning Comments News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer , Bethan Finigh It was an emotional day across Greater Manchester as thousands of students finally discovered their GCSE results, with nervous faces turning to smiles, tears and celebrations as they opened their long-awaited envelopes on Thursday (August 20) morning The day they had been waiting for comes just a week after a successful A Level Results Day , when students across the region celebrated a string of momentous successes Here at the Manchester Evening News , we travelled across Greater Manchester to meet some of the hardworking students behind the results, capturing the nerves, excitement and sheer relief as they ripped open their brown envelopes and discovered their futures The day painted a mixed picture across Greater Manchester. Trafford became the only area ranked in England's top 20 that is outside the south with a huge 39.7% of grades received by pupils in the borough of 7 or above Meanwhile, Rochdale was one of the worst performing councils with 13.2% at a grade 7 or above. Elsewhere across Greater Manchester, Salford was at 18.1%, Stockport 24.8%, Oldham 16.7%, Bolton 20.1% and Manchester 22.5%

Nearly three quarters (72.1%) of all grades were seven or above. That’s A or A* in traditional grades Richmond upon Thames had the next best results with 43.4% achieving a grade seven or higher. evidence_packet.evidence_text: GCSE results mapped as Greater Manchester borough named fifth best in England - see how your area ranks One Greater Manchester Manchester borough had the fifth best GCSE results in the country Comments News David Dubas-Fisher and Ryan Price 12:59, 20 As teenagers all over the country learned their GCSE results this morning (Thursday, 20 August), we're taking a look at how Greater Manchester schools compared to other parts of the country The City of London had the best GCSE results in the country this year. Nearly three quarters (72.1%) of all grades were seven or above. That’s A or A* in traditional grades Richmond upon Thames had the next best results with 43.4% achieving a grade seven or higher. That’s followed by fellow London boroughs of Sutton at 43.0% and Kingston upon Thames at 42.5% Trafford in Greater Manchester had the fifth best results in the country, however. With 39.7% achieving a grade 7 or above, it’s the highest score outside of the south of England by some distance You have to go all the way down to 51st place to find the next highest council outside of the south with Rutland at 28.3%. The next highest in the North is York with 27.0%

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Wigan residents hail extraordinary victory after council U-turns on masterplan - but this was 'just one battle' Bridgewater West has been removed from a local plan - meaning a scheme to turn it into a giant Wigan business park could be scrapped Campaigners say ‘the fight isn’t over’ after Wigan Council U-turned on plans to free up former greenbelt land in Astley for a huge business park Bridgewater West was tipped to become the home of around 540,000 sq ft of ‘employment space’ under the council’s Local Plan. Peel Group, which owns the land, planned to turn the area into a ‘ campus style’ business park, alongside new homes and a Park and Ride Campaigners have opposed the scheme from the start , arguing the open fields separating Astley and Boothstown are ‘vital’ to the local community and wildlife as well as protection from flooding. After a year of disputes, Wigan bosses have now rowed back on the scheme Four ‘controversial’ sites will be removed from the local plan. The document was due to be greenlit for public consultation at a cabinet meeting on Thursday, August 27. However now, The Bell, north of Junction 26, the Moss Industrial Estate extension, a pocket of land West of Win Joanna Allsopp, a high school teacher campaigning for the protection of the land , said the shift was a ‘positive step’

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police On the streets with the cops trying to tackle one of Manchester's biggest problems The 'game changing' technology is helping GMP cut down on anti-social behaviour and crime associated with e-bikes and e-scooters Comments News On a car park in north Manchester, a group of police officers are sat in a van huddled around a screen A bird's eye view of Harpurhey is being livestreamed directly from one of Greater Manchester Police's (GMP) drones onto the monitor. The officers have intel from a civilian about a lead they're after The drone is hovering over an address and, as soon as the video confirms their suspicions, officers on the ground are sent in and three arrests are made Moments earlier, a specially trained officer stood with his remote control in the car park, sending the drone off into the sky. Now, three men are sat in the back of a police van after GMP seized a stolen bike and subsequently found a machete in the house View 4 Images The drones are also used at events like concerts or football matches (Image: Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport man puzzled as latest bizarre bin incident caught on doorbell camera What Dave Bresnahan later found out, he said, had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporte In recent weeks, a furore of bin collections across the town and its suburbs has sent residents and councillors into a frenzy. Hundreds of bins went uncollected due to their lids being 'open' by millimetres in July, while a row ensued over the council's apparent crackdown on its Now in the latest strange happenings, resident Dave Bresnahan was left baffled by what was caught on his doorbell camera. Mr Bresnahan said it had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough The resident of Bosden Farm near Hazel Grove told the Manchester Evening News : “I had just gone down to the shops. We have had all this chaos about the bins all over Stockport . It’s been going on and on and on and everyone has got absolutely fed up “What happened was I put the bin out and I had been away for a few days. I came back that morning and I thought I would only put the black bin out because the rest weren’t full.” He added: “I went to the shop to get some milk and the blue bin was out. I thought that was a bit strange. I thought maybe the neighbour had put it out.”

candidates.evidence_text: Crime I stood and watched as GMP raided four new homes at 5am - four things stayed with me "It’s easy to forget the destructive criminality that is the reason for these raids - and the people whose lives it is blighting" Comments News opinion Greta Si I always say to anyone asking about my job that there are highs, and there are lows Highs might be the satisfaction of getting a really complex story over the line; reading positive feedback; a ticket to a show or artist you’ve been dying to see (contingent on a review, of course) All those things felt very far away, standing in the driving rain at 5.30am on August 20, watching a tactical aid officer saw through someone’s front door like a hot knife through butter We were on Hopwood Street in Pendlebury with officers from GMP’s Tactical Aid Unit and the Salford Neighbourhood team, watching them execute four dawn raids on properties suspected to be linked to drug dealing and burglaries in the area, with a fifth taking place in Clifton nearb It meant setting my alarm for 4am, hastily downing a coffee and a muffin on the rain-lashed M60 and rolling into a Salford police station just before 5am

candidates.evidence_text: Cheadle and Cheadle Hulme School opens doors for milestone event for children's charity Rainbow Trust The charity supports the families of children with life-threatenng and terminal illnesses, but doesn't receive any central government funding. News D A Greater Manchester school played host to a special celebration for a charity that has been helping families who have a child with life-threatening or terminal illnesses for the past 40 years. The Rainbow Trust, a children's care charity, hosted a special family fun day at Brads The charity has been established nationally for 40 years, and for 22 years has had its own Manchester Care team supporting local families. Joining the celebration was inspirational fundraiser Dr Michael Josephson MBE , who has raised £500,000 for the Rainbow Trust at his charity The event was an opportunity for those families supported by Rainbow Trust to come together and enjoy some much needed family fun during the school holidays. Children played alongside their siblings and families, and got to enjoy face painting, a treasure hunt, games, arts and cr Among those at the event were Evie and her family, who have been helped by the Rainbow Trust. Evie’s mum Vicky said: "As parents we are caring for Evie 24/7 and having support from Rainbow Trust brings Evie so much joy. Evie was born at 29 weeks and has been very poorly having ha "Without Rainbow Trust and Family Support Worker Emma’s support, life would be a lot more difficult."

Joining the celebration was inspirational fundraiser Dr Michael Josephson MBE , who has raised £500,000 for the Rainbow Trust at his charity The event was an opportunity for those families supported by Rainbow Trust to come together and enjoy some much needed family fun during the school holidays. candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale Partner of man, 31, found dead in Rochdale says 'I want him to be remembered as he was' as murder probe dropped Nathan Haigh died at a flat on Great Howarth on August 11 News Paul Britton Reporter and Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news repo The partner of a man who was found dead at a flat in Rochdale has described him as being 'like the sunshine' in a tribute for him Nathan Haigh, 31, was found unresponsive by emergency services at a flat on Great Howarth, near Wardle, just before 7.40pm last Tuesday (August 11). Police were initially called to the scene over reports of an 'unexpected death' Following Mr Haigh's death, a 37-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder . Detectives said they were exploring 'several lines of enquiries in what initially appeared to be suspicious circumstances' In an update issued on August 19, a Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said that 'following extensive enquiries, detectives have ruled out murder as a line of enquiry.' The woman arrested for murder was released and remains on bail for assault Rebecca Hamer, 36, has now shared a tribute for Mr Haigh. She said she was living with him at the time of his death after they struck up a recent relationship

candidates.evidence_text: GCSE results LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 18 hours ago GCSE Results Day 2026 RECAP as schools reach record-breaking grades Results and reaction from schools across the region as students find out their GCSE grades GCSE exam results at The Barlow RC High, On Thursday (August 20), 15 and 16-year-olds who sat their exams in May and June discovered whether they got the grades they needed for A levels, T levels, BTECs or apprenticeships Across the UK, the proportion of GCSE entries awarded top grades has risen from last year but the rate scoring a decent pass has returned to pre-pandemic levels. In north-west England, 18.9% of entries received grade 7 or above, up slightly from 18.8% in 2025 The results were made available to schools on Wednesday (August 19) and have been available to collect from schools from 8am. Schools across Greater Manchester have issued their own guidance on how and when students can collect results The grading system for GCSE results were revamped back in 2017 and now use a numbered system, replacing the traditional A* to G letter results. According to Ofqual, a grade 7 is comparable the old grade A; a grade 4 to the old C grade and the new grade 1 to the old grade G. Here Employers, universities and others who previously set entry requirements of at least a grade C, would now be at least a grade 4. Students who receive a grade 3 or below in GCSE maths or English language will generally have to continue studying the subject

candidates.lead: GCSE results Greater Manchester pupils celebrate GCSE results as one borough shines brightest and schools secure record-breaking year GCSE pupils received their grades this morning Comments News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer , Bethan Finigh It was an emotional day acro
candidates.evidence_text: GCSE results Greater Manchester pupils celebrate GCSE results as one borough shines brightest and schools secure record-breaking year GCSE pupils received their grades this morning Comments News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer , Bethan Finigh It was an emotional day across Greater Manchester as thousands of students finally discovered their GCSE results, with nervous faces turning to smiles, tears and celebrations as they opened their long-awaited envelopes on Thursday (August 20) morning The day they had been waiting for comes just a week after a successful A Level Results Day , when students across the region celebrated a string of momentous successes Here at the Manchester Evening News , we travelled across Greater Manchester to meet some of the hardworking students behind the results, capturing the nerves, excitement and sheer relief as they ripped open their brown envelopes and discovered their futures The day painted a mixed picture across Greater Manchester. Trafford became the only area ranked in England's top 20 that is outside the south with a huge 39.7% of grades received by pupils in the borough of 7 or above Meanwhile, Rochdale was one of the worst performing councils with 13.2% at a grade 7 or above. Elsewhere across Greater Manchester, Salford was at 18.1%, Stockport 24.8%, Oldham 16.7%, Bolton 20.1% and Manchester 22.5%

candidates.evidence_text: GCSE results mapped as Greater Manchester borough named fifth best in England - see how your area ranks One Greater Manchester Manchester borough had the fifth best GCSE results in the country Comments News David Dubas-Fisher and Ryan Price 12:59, 20 As teenagers all over the country learned their GCSE results this morning (Thursday, 20 August), we're taking a look at how Greater Manchester schools compared to other parts of the country The City of London had the best GCSE results in the country this year. Nearly three quarters (72.1%) of all grades were seven or above. That’s A or A* in traditional grades Richmond upon Thames had the next best results with 43.4% achieving a grade seven or higher. That’s followed by fellow London boroughs of Sutton at 43.0% and Kingston upon Thames at 42.5% Trafford in Greater Manchester had the fifth best results in the country, however. With 39.7% achieving a grade 7 or above, it’s the highest score outside of the south of England by some distance You have to go all the way down to 51st place to find the next highest council outside of the south with Rutland at 28.3%. The next highest in the North is York with 27.0%

Charities give their verdicts, as the Prime Minister announces he wants to get people off the streets by Christmas View 9 Images Comments News I As well as his insistence that he would bring the welfare budget down and honour the UK’s defence commitments abroad, his first pledge was to tackle the homelessness crisis “I will soon go through that door behind me and issue my first instruction – to end rough sleeping in our country. It’s about putting the right values and the right standards at the heart of government,” he told the nation. “I will put the care of people at the heart of everythin Some £340 million funding was announced to go towards acquiring suitable homes, identifying those most in need and starting to provide housing and support ‘without delay’ The funding will provide 1,200 homes and intensive support for at least 3,000 long-term rough sleepers over a five-year period, the Government said The latest annual national statistics, published by the Government in February, estimated that 4,793 people were sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2025 in England. That was a new record and the fourth annual increase in a row

But now, as NHS treatment options dwindle, Sarah has turned to fundraising for private care Sarah said: “It blew our world apart,” recalling her diagnosis in 2019 She added: “I’ve lived with it now for seven years. I’m eternally grateful to The Christie, but we’ve come to a point now where they can’t offer me anything else under the NHS. My team are as frustrated as I am.” Sarah believes the drug Enhertu could help her, but while it is available to NHS patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer in Scotland, it is not yet offered in England

candidates.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

candidates.evidence_text: Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Hospital, was put under an NHS enforcement notice to improve patient safety, in June But whistle blowers have now told an investigation by the Independent and Channel 4 that they were discouraged from reporting concerns The trust has told the BBC it is working to address staff concerns and has "clear processes to investigate incidents" A spokesperson for NCA said the trust changed the way it was organised in response to demands by NHS England to improve standards in surgical wards, tackling backlogs in spinal and gynaecology services But the investigation found patients are alleged to have been "left dying or in pain" in overcrowded A&E corridors, before then receiving invasive treatments which might have been avoided if there was no delay, the investigation claims Other allegations raised in the report include staff suggesting their accounts of serious harm or death are "shut down or not investigated properly"

candidates.source_evidence: Manchester saw more homes built in the last year (4,766) than all the 32 Greater London boroughs combined (4,261) a report to the Council’s Communities and Equalities Scrutiny Committee heard today (Weds 22 July) The significant achievement marks another record-breaking year as part of the Council’s ambitious housing strategy up to 2032, which also saw more affordable homes built than at any point since the late 1990s with 901 affordable tenure homes completed – of which around half (439) Manchester is also bucking the national trend for affordable housing starts recording an increase of 12% since 2022/23 And the city centre also saw the largest ever delivery of affordable in the city’s history over the last year with 259 completions, helping to diversify the city centre housing market and help more Manchester people have more choice about where they live The Housing Strategy update shows that the city remains on track to meet its target to deliver at least 36,000 homes of all tenures by 2032, including 10,000 social, Council and genuinely affordable homes – 3,000 of which will be in the city centre 13,555 homes have already been delivered since 2022 with more than 7,800 currently under construction, and a further 20,000 homes with planning approval or in the pipeline

evidence_packet.evidence_text: More children in Rochdale will have access to a free breakfast before school from September after 7 local schools successfully applied to the national breakfast club programme The initiative provides primary-aged pupils with a healthy and nutritious meal before school to help them get off to the best possible start before a full day of learning It also helps parents and carers with extra childcare at the start of the school day, with children arriving at school up to 30 minutes earlier at no extra cost Schools joining the programme include Shawclough Community Primary School, Sandbrook Community Primary School, St John's Roman Catholic Primary School and Heybrook Primary School Deeplish Primary Academy, Holy Family Roman Catholic Primary School and Moorhouse Academy are also involved Their inclusion brings the total number of local schools participating in the programme up to 10, with Bamford Academy, Broadfield Community Primary School and Springside already enlisted

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Council is launching a new licensing scheme for landlords of houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) The scheme is designed to improve property conditions, strengthen management standards, and ensure tenants have access to safe, high-quality accommodation and was agreed at a meeting of Bolton Council’s Cabinet on Monday (August 17) HMOs are properties that are occupied by three or more people from different households, who share at least one basic amenity i.e. a kitchen, bathroom or toilet - the definition includes bedsits, shared houses and some self–contained flats that did not meet the required standard It is unacceptable that landlords cut corners in critical areas such as failing to obtain fire, gas, and electrical safety certificates or ensuring properties are safe Many landlords operate responsibly, but a substantial proportion of HMOs are poorly managed, unsafe and impact on the community In the past three years, the council has received 1,885 complaints about disrepair in rented homes, typically relating to fire safety, electrical and structural defects, overcrowding, cold and damp, and poor waste management and pest control

By removing them from the latest version of the Local Plan, we believe we have struck the right balance between supporting economic growth and job creation, providing opportunities for residents, and protecting ou With Gibfield, we simply do not believe the proposals are appropriate and we will make that clear through the consultation. The masterplan requires the council's approval and we cannot support it.”

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. candidates.evidence_text: Grub on the Docks - Media City UK Street Food Line-Up: Featuring Sizzling Seoul, Dukes Po Boys, and more Grub on the Docks Venue Gardens Dates 28 th May - 20 th Sep '26 Open Tuesday to Sunday weekly, 12 noon – 10pm GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront. We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try. NEW challenge, take on the BELLY BUSTER CHALLENGE from CAFF – sausage. bacon. egg. black pudding. hash brown. All packed into one proper Belly Buster bap for £7.50. Time to beat is 5 minutes set the fastest finishing time and your next Belly Buster is FREE . EVENTS Wine on the Docks Every Wednesday | All day, venue hours Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day. Sunset Sessions Every Friday | 5–8pm Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted. Paws on the Docks 8 AUGUST | 22 AUGUST | 5 SEPTEMBER | 19 SEPTEMBER | Mornings Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones. Residents social Thursday 20th August – 5pm to 7pm An evening for all MediaCity residents, with a DJ playing live on the docks. A nice informal social, come down, grab a drink and meet other residents at our waterfront setting. Media Makers Mixer Thursday 27th August – 5pm to 7pm A regular hosted networking event for MediaCity’s creative and production community, designed to bring people together and encourage connections across the area. Be the first in the know Sign up to receive email updates on the latest events, news and offers at MediaCity Visit our privacy policy here. Welcome to The Bolly-woods, where the dancing is non-stop, the drama is bigger than your aunties, and the romance is straight out of a filmi blockbuster! Meet Surinder, sweet, strong, and stuck in a never-ending chore list thanks to her two Insta-fame obsessed stepsisters, Lovely and Bubbly. Her only real support? The one and only Basanti, a cow with the dance skills of Bollywood superstar! Meanwhile, Prince Kavi is drowning in marriage pressure from his royal family. But when he accidentally bumps into Surinder, sparks fly. Enter the fabulous Devi Godmother played by Harpz Kaur (BBC Asian Network, CBBC's Saturday Mash-up). She'll be arriving in full-on glam mode with magic, makeovers, and masala moves. An all singing, all dancing Bollywood revamp of beloved family classic Cinderella With a dazzling Bollywood Ball, a mystical slipper, and a lot of drama, Surinder’s destiny is about to get a serious glow-up! Book your tickets now, before midnight strikes! A delightful blend of storytelling, music, dance and humour. A fine example of the way diversity enriches our culture. Surinderella showcases authentic, joyful visibility and representation Buy direct from venues with ATG Tickets. Transparent booking fees, no late stage surprises. The Palace Theatre of Varieties opened on Whit Monday 1891 and cost its owners the then colossal sum of £40,500. In the late 1970’s the Palace Theatre underwent a major refurbishment and re-opened in 1981 with Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Jesus Christ Superstar and has since then retained its position as the premier provincial touring venue

candidates.evidence_text: ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Павел Дедищев выступит в Лондоне со своим стендап концертом "АМЕРИКАНЕЦ" Лондон! 30го сентября к нам приезжает Павел Дедищев со своим концертом "Американец" Резидент шоу Stand Up на ТНТ, финалист «Comedy Баттл» и «Большого шоу», участник проектов «Решалы» и «Было слово». Он стоял у истоков объединения HIT2SHIT (будущего Labelcom), стал сооснователем канала «Комьюнити» и одним из тех, кто формировал новую волну русскоязычного стендапа. Павел Дедищев - комик с ярко выраженным собственным стилем, в котором сочетаются честность, дерзость и умение подмечать детали, знакомые каждому. Его стендап строится на живых наблюдениях, бытовых историях и неожиданных поворотах, которые превращают обычные ситуации в мощные комедийные моменты. Дедищев говорит прямо, не сглаживает углы и именно этим вызывает у зрителей тот самый взрывной смех. Address: Big Belly Comedy Club, Unit 6 & 7, 30 Stamford St, London SE1 9LQ Doors: 19:00 Start: 19:45 End: 21:30 Мы работаем по принципу first come, first served, а именно, кто пришел раньше, то и занял лучшее место. 18+ P.S. So is most of the menu, to be honest. Visitors are strongly encouraged to come along to eat, drink and vote !

candidates.evidence_text: Totally Stockport has launched a new masterplan as part of its Going Green programme, setting out a bold and practical vision for a greener, healthier and more vibrant town centre Developed by Layer.studio in consultation with retailers and residents, ‘Going Green’ focuses on the places people use every day and sets out a strategy, toolkit and initial projects to support regeneration, wellbeing and economic activity With the aim to create a connected, people-focused green infrastructure network, streets, squares and key routes have been reviewed to create a one connected green network The masterplan spans the 80Ha Totally Stockport BID Boundary and combines quick wins with longer-term visions in key areas, setting out a practical route to a town centre that’s even more walkable, attractive and economically active Paul Kelsall, BID Director at Totally Stockport and co-owner of Stockport based Kelsall Architects, said: “At its core, ‘Going Green’ is about joining the green dots “From Merseyway to the Underbanks and Chestergate, the masterplan shows how simple, well-placed changes such as more planting and enhanced greenery can change the face of the town centre

candidates.practical_angle: Есть обновление, которое может быть полезно в сегодняшней сводке.
candidates.lead: JD Sports has cut its full-year profit forecast after sales fell during a challenging second quarter, with weakness in North America and footwear weighing on the Bury-headquartered retail giant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: The Northern heat of the prestigious British Street Food Awards Stockport Covered Market Hall , Manchester 23 August 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Stockport Market has spent the best part of a decade becoming a very good reason to visit this fast-growing town, and Foodie Friday is the crux of it all. Last Friday of every month, several thousand people turn up with hungry bellies and cash to splash Naturally, higher-ups have taken note, and now we have the biggest event yet: a Northern heat of the British Street Food Awards, held this Sunday, 23 August, from noon to six It’s what we like to call something of a big deal : twenty traders whittled out of 3,000 applicants – roughly the same odds as getting into Oxbridge, all competing for a lot in the national final. You can (and should) spend your Sunday sampling their wares. Wear those pants with We’re not sure about other heats – Northern pride tells us they’re all suckers – but they’d have to go some way to top this judging panel line-up: Sam Buckley of Where the Light Gets In ; Holly Temple of Filler zine; and Joe McGrath, podcast host and the voice of BBC Radio Manche

candidates.lead: Наталка Карпа at Brixton Jamm
candidates.evidence_text: 17 октября 2026 года в Brixton Jamm состоится концерт Наталки Карпы в Лондоне В Лондоне прозвучит украинская песня, и снова найдет своих людей, ведь на сцену выйдет Наталка Карпа — певица, чей голос уже более двух десятилетий остается голосом света и искренней любви к родной земле. Для многих украинцев за границей ее концерт станет не только художественным Наталья Карпа получила два высших образования, однако именно музыка стала делом ее жизни. От первых фестивалей и конкурсов до больших сцен Украины и мира, от песни “Калина”, открывшей ей путь к широкому признанию, до многочисленных сольных концертов и международных туров для укра Заслуженная артистка Украины, автор десятков популярных композиций, продюсер и общественный деятель в своем репертуаре легко сочетает лирическую нежность и праздничную энергию, а рядом с хорошо известными хитами непременно звучат новые композиции. Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость. Музыка преодолевает расстояния, находит дорогу к сердцу независимо от того, где человек живет сегодня, и оставляет после себя огонь жизни! Чтобы попасть на концерт Наталки Карпы в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города. Еще больше концертов в афише Лондона ищите у нас на сайте

Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы.
